purpose: Concrete teaching examples for interpreting operator labels without changing live policy.

examples.label: correct_hold
examples.scenario: Range environment, price mid-range, spread wide, macro conflict present.
examples.why: Movement after the fact does not make the original decision executable.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Reinforce patience and avoid hindsight bias.

examples.label: correct_hold
examples.scenario: Liquidity sweep appears, but no structure reclaim and no reversal momentum confirmation.
examples.why: Sweep alone is not a reversal setup.

examples.label: too_cautious
examples.scenario: Clear HH/HL uptrend, pullback into structure, momentum turns back up, spread normal, macro neutral/supportive, but Atlas still holds.
examples.why: The playbook was clean enough for existing gates to review.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Investigate whether confidence or same-side support is lagging.

examples.label: missed_trade
examples.scenario: Breakout retest holds cleanly with follow-through, no event risk, acceptable execution, and Atlas does not produce a directional candidate.
examples.why: The setup matched a known playbook and execution conditions were usable.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Review setup recognition and confirmation timing.

examples.label: bad_setup
examples.scenario: Atlas likes continuation while price is in chop, momentum weak, and no pullback or breakout location is present.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Tighten setup recognition, not risk policy.

examples.label: correct_hold
examples.scenario: M1 structure is LH/LL, price is mid-range, momentum is mixed, and Atlas has a buy candidate with only one supporting signal.
examples.why: The candidate direction is not the same as entry permission; the buy idea needs reversal proof, structure reclaim, or stronger same-side support.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Classify this as developing/no-trade until confirmation improves.

examples.label: bad_setup
examples.scenario: Atlas treats a mid-range mixed-momentum move as continuation because confidence is above threshold.
examples.why: Confidence without clean location, momentum confirmation, and sufficient consensus is not a complete setup.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Do not promote mid-range movement into an executable setup.

examples.label: correct_hold
examples.scenario: Trend structure is visible, but the candidate has weak or mixed momentum, mid-range or unclear entry location, late-session/wide-spread execution friction, or DXY/US10Y macro conflict.
examples.why: Trend direction and entry permission are separate. A trade can be directionally plausible and still be too weak to execute.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Classify this as developing/no-trade until momentum confirms, location improves, and execution/macro conditions stop fighting the setup.

examples.label: bad_setup
examples.scenario: After recent losses, Atlas tries to repeat a continuation, pullback, or breakout idea in the same weak-momentum, poor-location, wide-spread, or macro-conflicted context.
examples.why: The loss cluster is teaching Atlas that these conditions are vulnerable to poor timing, not that it should loosen guards or force trades.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Haircut confidence and explain the missing confirmation before any execution review.

examples.label: execution_issue
examples.scenario: A setup is recognized, but execution truth reports broker confirmation missing, rejection, timeout, or reconciliation required.
examples.why: Broker/routing failure is separate from strategy quality.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Classify the failure cause from execution_truth before blaming setup logic.

examples.label: execution_issue
examples.scenario: Setup is recognizable, but spread/liquidity/slippage/session conditions are unsafe.
examples.why: The trade idea and execution environment are separate problems.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Keep the setup insight but do not treat poor execution as strategy failure.

examples.label: confusing_answer
examples.scenario: Operator asks about capabilities, learning, or limitations and Atlas answers with HOLD/PAPER/RUN status.
examples.why: The answer is irrelevant even if the status is true.
examples.atlas_should_learn: Route self-knowledge and learning questions to Brain v2 knowledge, not trading-state fallback.

policy_note: Examples are teaching references only. They do not authorize automatic strategy, risk, or execution changes.
